ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Above the horizontal ground there are perpendicular uniform electric and magnetic fields; the direction of the uniform electric field is vertically downward, and the direction of the uniform magnetic field is horizontally inward. Now a positively charged metal ball is thrown horizontally from point M with initial velocity $v_0$. When the ball lands, its velocity is $v_1$, and its flight time in the air is $t_1$. If the magnetic field is removed while all other conditions remain unchanged, then when the ball lands its velocity is $v_2$, and its flight time in the air is $t_2$. Air resistance on the ball can be neglected. Then regarding the comparison of the magnitudes of $v_1$ and $v_2$, $t_1$ and $t_2$, which of the following judgments is correct? ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Flight time relation
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Under the same conditions: when there is a magnetic field, the flight time of the ball in the air is $t_1$; after the magnetic field is removed, the flight time is $t_2$. Neglecting air resistance, compare the magnitude relation between $t_1$ and $t_2$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Under the same conditions: when there is a magnetic field, the flight time of the ball in the air is $t_1$; after the magnetic field is removed, the flight time is $t_2$. Neglecting air resistance, compare the magnitude relation between $t_1$ and $t_2$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure the ball is at point M, thrown horizontally to the right from point M with initial velocity v0; the ground is below; the direction of electric field E is vertically downward; the magnetic field is represented by cross marks, with direction perpendicular to the paper surface inward; the ball is positively charged. Reasoning: When the magnetic field is removed, in the vertical direction the ball is subject only to gravity mg and the downward electric force qE, so the vertically downward acceleration is constantly a2=g+qE/m, and the initial vertical velocity is 0. When there is a magnetic field, the positively charged ball has initial velocity horizontally to the right, and the magnetic field direction is inward; from qv×B it can be known that the magnetic force is initially vertically upward. During the motion, the horizontal velocity of the ball remains to the right, therefore the magnetic force always has an upward vertical component, which will offset part of the gravity and electric force, making the effective vertically downward acceleration of the ball smaller than the acceleration when the magnetic field is removed. In both cases the ball is thrown from the same height, and the initial vertical velocity is both 0; if the vertical falling acceleration is smaller, the time required to reach the ground is longer. Therefore the flight time is longer when there is a magnetic field.

method.method_draft: 从图中读出：小球从 M 点以水平向右初速度抛出，电场 E 竖直向下，磁场 B 垂直纸面向里，地面在下方。由文字读出：小球带正电，忽略空气阻力，比较有磁场飞行时间 t1 与撤去磁场飞行时间 t2。先分析撤去磁场时，竖直方向只有重力和向下电场力，竖直向下加速度为恒定的 g+qE/m。再分析有磁场时，正电荷水平向右运动且 B 向里，由左手定则或 qv×B 可知磁场力初始竖直向上；运动过程中小球水平速度始终向右，因此磁场力始终有向上的竖直分量，抵消部分重力和电场力，使竖直向下的有效加速度小于撤去磁场时。相同高度、初始竖直速度均为零，竖直下落加速度较小者落地时间更长，所以 t1＞t2。
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中小球位于 M 点，从 M 点以初速度 v0 水平向右抛出；地面在下方；电场 E 方向竖直向下；磁场用叉号表示，方向垂直纸面向里；小球带正电。
推理：撤去磁场时，小球竖直方向只受重力 mg 和向下电场力 qE，因此竖直向下加速度恒为 a2=g+qE/m，初始竖直速度为 0。有磁场时，正电小球初速度水平向右，磁场方向向里，由 qv×B 可知磁场力初始竖直向上。运动过程中小球的水平速度保持向右，因此磁场力始终具有向上的竖直分量，这会抵消一部分重力和电场力，使小球竖直向下的有效加速度小于撤去磁场时的加速度。两种情况下小球从同一高度抛出，初始竖直速度都为 0；竖直下落加速度较小，则到达地面所需时间较长。因此有磁场时飞行时间更长。
